    AgentBasedLotkaVolterraSystem(width=30, height=30, *, prey=300, predators=60, birth=0.2, conversion=0.5, death=0.1, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Prey and predators that walk on a grid, whose numbers cycle.

    Their numbers cycle like the Lotka-Volterra equations.

    Prey give birth only in cells they do not share with other prey, which limits their density, and predators eat prey they meet and breed after a meal. Demographic noise makes the cycles irregular and can end them by extinction. The system has the groups prey and predators.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    width int

    The number of columns of the torus.

    		 30
    height int

    The number of rows of the torus.

    		 30
    prey int

    The initial number of prey.

    		 300
    predators int

    The initial number of predators.

    		 60
    birth float

    The probability that a prey gives birth at every step.

    		 0.2
    conversion float

    The probability that a predator breeds after eating a prey.

    		 0.5
    death float

    The probability that a predator dies at every step.

    		 0.1
    random_state int | Generator | None

    The seed or generator of the initial cells.

    		 0
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import AgentBasedLotkaVolterraSystem
>>> system = AgentBasedLotkaVolterraSystem(10, 10, prey=50, predators=5).prepare().system_
>>> [group.size for group in system.elements]
[50, 5]

    CometsSystem(shape=(50, 50), *, box=0.02, inoculum=3e-07, glucose=5.0, plate_glucose=0.0088, biomass_diffusion=3e-10, glucose_diffusion=5e-06, vmax=10.0, km=0.01, interval=STEP, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    An expanding colony of the E. coli core system on a lattice.

    It needs the extra metabolism.

    Run with IMEXEulerSolver, every step is a growth step and then a diffusion step, the two steps that COMETS alternates (Raman 2021, Section 11.1.3.4). The growth step solves the program of every site that holds biomass and applies the update rules of Harcombe et al. (2014). The diffusion step solves one implicit Euler system, where Harcombe et al. use an alternating direction implicit scheme. Biomass and glucose both diffuse, as in Harcombe et al., while the short description of Raman names metabolites only.

    The states are gDW per L and mM of the medium under a box. A site whose program has no solution has zero fluxes, which happens when its glucose cannot pay for the maintenance flux of the network.

    Harcombe et al. in what follows is the main text of Harcombe et al. (2014), and the source of each default is named under its argument. The time step of 0.1 h of the registered run is from its In silico experiments. The length of the registered run keeps it within the budget of the gallery and has no source.

    These choices have no source in that text. The periodic edges are those of LatticeSpace, since the text does not state the outer boundary. The volume under a box is the amount of glucose under it over the concentration of the medium, since the text defers the volume to its supplement, which was not read. The molar mass of glucose is 180.16 g/mol.

    The network is the E. coli core system, where Harcombe et al. use iJO1366. The death rate of 1% per step, the largest colony height of 200 um, and the oxygen of 0.25 mmol/cm^2 of Harcombe et al. are left out, so the biomass of a box has no upper limit and oxygen is limited only by the network.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    shape tuple[int, int]

    The number of boxes along each side, by default from Harcombe et al., Colony expansion comparisons.

    		 (50, 50)
    box float

    The side of a box in cm, by default from Harcombe et al., Colony expansion comparisons.

    		 0.02
    inoculum float

    The initial biomass of the central box in g, by default from Harcombe et al., Colony expansion comparisons.

    		 3e-07
    glucose float

    The glucose of the medium in g/L, by default from Harcombe et al., In silico experiments.

    		 5.0
    plate_glucose float

    The glucose of the medium per area of the plate in mmol/cm^2, by default from Harcombe et al., In silico experiments.

    		 0.0088
    biomass_diffusion float

    The diffusion coefficient of the biomass in cm^2/s, by default the value for colonies from Harcombe et al., Table 1.

    		 3e-10
    glucose_diffusion float

    The diffusion coefficient of the glucose in cm^2/s, by default from Harcombe et al., Table 1.

    		 5e-06
    vmax float

    The largest glucose uptake in mmol/g/h, by default from Harcombe et al., Table 1.

    		 10.0
    km float

    The half-saturation concentration of glucose in mM, by default from Harcombe et al., Table 1.

    		 0.01
    interval float

    The time in h over which the glucose of a site must last, by default the time step, the bound of Raman (2021, Section 9.6).

    		 STEP
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    Raises:

    Type Description
    MissingExtraError

    The extra is not installed.

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import CometsSystem
>>> [element.label for element in CometsSystem(shape=(2, 2)).prepare().system_.elements]
['cells', 'biomass', 'glucose']

    CommunityFBASystem(knockouts=('ICDHyr', 'NH4t'), *, abundances=(0.5, 0.5), exchanges=None, common_rate=False, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Two members of the E. coli core system that share a medium.

    It needs the extra metabolism.

    The programs of the members merge through a medium whose law holds the growth weighted by the abundances (Raman 2021, Section 11.1.3). By default one member lacks isocitrate dehydrogenase and takes up 2-oxoglutarate, and the other lacks ammonium transport and takes up glutamate, each from what the other secretes, so neither grows alone, and together both grow. community_growth gives SteadyCom and the cooperative trade-off of the same members. The pair is an illustration found on the E. coli core system: the consortium of Raman (Section 11.1.3.6) has four mutants that need amino acids, whose synthesis the core system does not hold.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    knockouts Sequence[str]

    The reaction to close in each member, or the empty string for none.

    		 ('ICDHyr', 'NH4t')
    abundances Sequence[float]

    The abundance of each member.

    		 (0.5, 0.5)
    exchanges Mapping[str, float] | None

    The lower bound of the net exchange of the community, by reaction, or None for no net uptake of the cross-fed metabolites.

    		 None
    common_rate bool

    Whether the members grow at one specific rate, as in community FBA, rather than each at its own, as in joint FBA.

    		 False
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    Raises:

    Type Description
    MissingExtraError

    The extra is not installed.

    Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import CommunityFBASystem
>>> trajectory = simulate(CommunityFBASystem(), until=0.0)
>>> round(float(trajectory.values('medium.objective_0')[0]), 3)
0.862

    CompetitionInteraction(label, *, first, second, r1=1.0, r2=1.0, K1=100.0, K2=100.0, alpha12=0.5, alpha21=0.5)

    Bases: Interaction

    Lotka-Volterra competition of two species for the same resources.

    Each species grows logistically, and the other species fills its carrying capacity in proportion to a competition coefficient, dn1/dt = r1 n1 (1 - (n1 + alpha12 n2) / K1) and dn2/dt = r2 n2 (1 - (n2 + alpha21 n1) / K2).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the interaction.

    		 required
    first Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

    The path of the first population.

    		 required
    second Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

    The path of the second population.

    		 required
    r1 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The growth rate of the first population.

    		 1.0
    r2 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The growth rate of the second population.

    		 1.0
    K1 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=open(0, oo))]

    The carrying capacity of the first population.

    		 100.0
    K2 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=open(0, oo))]

    The carrying capacity of the second population.

    		 100.0
    alpha12 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The effect of one member of the second population on the first, relative to one of its own.

    		 0.5
    alpha21 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The effect of one member of the first population on the second, relative to one of its own.

    		 0.5

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import CompetitionInteraction
>>> CompetitionInteraction('competition', first='deer', second='elk', alpha12=0.5).alpha12

    CompetitionSystem(first=10.0, second=10.0, *, r1=1.0, r2=0.8, K1=100.0, K2=80.0, alpha12=0.5, alpha21=0.6, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Two species that compete for the same resources.

    They coexist or exclude each other.

    The species coexist at n1 = (K1 - alpha12 K2) / (1 - alpha12 alpha21) and n2 = (K2 - alpha21 K1) / (1 - alpha12 alpha21) when both are positive and alpha12 alpha21 < 1. Otherwise one species excludes the other. The system has the populations first and second.

    ConsumerResourceSystem(consumers=None, resources=None, *, c=UPTAKE, m=1.0, e=1.0, w=1.0, r=1.0, K=CAPACITIES, kappa=CAPACITIES, omega=1.0, supply='logistic', kind='substitutable', n=-10.0, v=None, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Consumer species that compete only through the resources they take up.

    It follows MacArthur's niche theory.

    The 'logistic' supply of substitutable resources is MacArthur's consumer-resource model, dN_i/dt = e_i N_i (sum_b w_b c_ib R_b - m_i) and dR_a/dt = r_a R_a (K_a - R_a) / K_a - sum_j c_ja N_j R_a. The 'chemostat' supply kappa_a - omega_a R_a models nutrients that flow in from outside, and essential resources limit growth jointly through (sum_b (c_ib R_b)^n)^(1/n), consumed by the stoichiometry v. At most as many consumers as resources coexist, at the point where their zero net growth isoclines g_i(R) = m_i cross. With the defaults, the settings of Mehta and Blumenthal (2024, figure 4), both consumers coexist at R = (5/3, 5/9), the point of the region where no consumer can invade that is closest to the supply point K.

    The competition for one resource of Gros (2015, exercise 8), dx_i/dt = (f r_i - d) x_i and df/dt = a - f sum_i r_i x_i, is the chemostat with one resource, c = r, m = d, kappa = a, and omega = 0. The total population tends to a / d, the resource to min_i d / r_i, and only the consumer with the largest r_i survives. The system has the populations consumers.N and the resources resources.R.

    ConsumptionInteraction(label, *, consumers, resources, c=((1.0,),), kind='substitutable', n=-10.0)

    Bases: Interaction

    Consumption of substitutable or essential resources by consumer species.

    Consumption is the only way the consumers interact.

    Consumer i takes up resource a at the rate c_ia R_a per individual. Substitutable resources add their energies w_b c_ib R_b, and essential resources all limit the growth, g_i = (sum_b (c_ib R_b)^n)^(1/n) for n < -1, which tends to Liebig's law g_i = min_b c_ib R_b as n goes to minus infinity. Its subclasses give the laws of the consumers and of the resources, which read the other group through reductions.

    DroopCellQuotaSystem(Q=1.5, P=1.0, *, r_inf=1.0, q=1.0, vmax=2.0, g=1.0, R=1.0, d=0.1, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The Droop system of a phytoplankton that grows on its stored nutrient.

    The growth rate of the phytoplankton follows the nutrient stored in its cells.

    The growth rate r_inf (1 - q / Q) rises with the quota Q and saturates at r_inf. Under a constant external nutrient the quota settles at Q* = q + v / r_inf, where v = vmax R / (g + R) is the uptake, and the biomass then grows exponentially at r_inf (1 - q / Q*) - d. The book gives no values for this system, so the defaults are in units of the minimum quota, the maximum growth rate, and the half saturation, with time in days. The system has the quota algae.Q and the biomass algae.P.

    DynamicMultispeciesFBASystem(*, fast_vmax=10.0, slow_vmax=8.0, biomass=0.01, glucose=10.0, km=0.015, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Two E. coli core strains that differ in maximal glucose uptake on one medium.

    It needs the extra metabolism.

    Each strain has its own program, uptake kinetics, and biomass, and they read one glucose pool (Raman 2021, Section 11.1.3.4). The strain with the larger uptake grows faster, so its share rises until the glucose runs out. The two strains and their uptakes of 10 and 8 are an illustration of the framework, whose example in the source is the competition between Rhodoferax and Geobacter (Zhuang et al. 2011).

    A food web of logistic basal species and Lotka-Volterra consumers.

    The basal species grow logistically and the consumers live on Lotka-Volterra predation.

    The default web has frogs and mice at its base, snakes that eat frogs and mice, and hawks that eat snakes and mice. Its four species coexist at a stable equilibrium. The system has one population per species.

    ForagerElement(label, visual=VisualSpec('agents', {'color_by': 'happiness', 'radius': 0.35}), *, age=0.0, hunger=0.0, happiness=0.0, distress=0.0, experience=0.0, maturity=5.0, reproduction=0.3, starvation=10.0, memory=0.3, communication=0.1, emotions=1.0)

    Bases: Element

    Animal that hunts its food guided by emotions, and breeds.

    The emotions are its own and those its kind left on the ground.

    Every step the animal ages and grows hungry, and starves when its hunger passes starvation. It moves to the neighbouring cell, empty or holding food, of highest preference: 1 for food, plus, with emotions, the happiness marked there minus its own and its own distress minus the distress marked there. It eats food it moves onto. Its emotions follow E' = (1 - memory) (X + communication C) + memory E, with the experience X of the step and the mean emotion C marked around it, and it marks its cell with them. A mature animal breeds into an empty neighbouring cell with a probability that happiness raises and distress lowers, and its offspring shares its hunger, so a lineage starves together when its food is gone. Subclasses name their food and the marks they read, and the system adds the ageing, the hunger, the starvation, the experience of distress, the move, the meal, the emotions, the marks, and the breeding as member interactions.

    ForestSizeStructureSystem(positions=40, heights=100, *, width=10.0, dispersal=1.0, hurst=1.0, sapling=0.1, top=50.0, shading=1.0, fecundity=0.01, resources=125.0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The McKendrick-von Foerster density of trees over position and height.

    The position runs across a strip.

    The density f(x, h) of trees of height h at position x across a forest strip grows in height at the rate I (1 - h / top), where the light I = exp(-shading int_h^top f(x, h') h'^(2H) dh') falls through the canopy of taller trees by the Beer-Lambert law. Trees die from competition for canopy space at the rate I h^(2H) f and for resources at the rate I (1 - h / top) a / h, where a = R / resources and R = int h^(1+2H) f dh is the resource consumption of the trees at x. Saplings enter at the height sapling from the seeds int K(x - x') R(x') dx' of the trees around, dispersed by the exponential kernel K of length dispersal and integral fecundity, and no seed comes from beyond the edges of the strip, where the forest was removed. Time and density are rescaled so that the growth rate and the canopy mortality are one (Grilletta et al. 2026, arXiv 2608.11918 Eq. 9, 10, 16, and 25). The kernel is the exponential of Eq. 35 along the axis across the strip, normalized in one dimension. The system has the density forest.f over position and height.

    GeneralizedLotkaVolterraInteraction(label, *, target, a=-1.0, state='x')

    Bases: CouplingInteraction

    Interactions of the species of a group, dx_i/dt += x_i sum_j a_ij x_j.

    They act through an interaction matrix a.

    Every species i couples to every species j of the group, itself included, through the term x_i x_j weighted by the entry a_ij of the interaction matrix, a parameter with one row and one column per species, so a schedule or an experiment changes it. The diagonal entries are the interactions of a species with itself, negative for self-limitation. With the growth b_i x_i as a rate, it gives the generalized Lotka-Volterra equations dx_i/dt = x_i (b_i + sum_j a_ij x_j).

    GeneralizedLotkaVolterraSystem(x=None, *, b=COMMUNITY_GROWTH, a=COMMUNITY_INTERACTIONS, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The generalized Lotka-Volterra system of a microbial community.

    It follows dx_i/dt = x_i (b_i + sum_j a_ij x_j).

    Every species grows at its intrinsic rate b_i and its growth changes with the abundance of every species through the pairwise interaction a_ij. A feasible interior fixed point solves b + a x = 0. The book gives no parameter values. The default is a choice, a community of three self-limiting species with weak competition and one weak mutualism, whose fixed point x = -a^-1 b is positive and stable, so the species coexist. Abundances and time are in arbitrary units. The system has the abundances species.x of the members of the group species, the growth growth, and the interactions glv, whose matrix is the parameter glv.a.

    def regrow(self, agent: GrassView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Count down eaten grass and grow it back when the countdown ends.

    Args:
        agent:
            The patch.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    del system
    if agent.grown:
        return
    agent.countdown -= 1
    if agent.countdown <= 0:
        agent.grown = 1.0
        agent.countdown = agent.regrowth

    HigherOrderRandomLotkaVolterraSystem(size=200, *, mu=-4.0, sigma=1.0, gamma=0.0, k=1.0, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    A random Lotka-Volterra community with third-order interactions.

    The abundances follow dx_i/dt = x_i (k - x_i + sum_(j<k) a_ijk x_j x_k) (Sidhom and Galla 2024, Eq. 2), where the sum runs over the pairs of other species. The coefficients are Gaussian with mean mu / binom(N - 1, 2) and variance 3 sigma^2 / (2 binom(N - 1, 2)), and the three coefficients of a set of three species have the correlation gamma (Eqs. 4 and 5). The defaults are the competitive community of the paper's Fig. 2, 200 species with uncorrelated coefficients at mu = -4 and sigma = 1, in its phase with a unique stable fixed point, where the theory gives a fraction 0.928 of surviving species and a mean abundance 0.392. The paper does not state the distribution of the initial abundances, which are drawn uniformly from the interval from 0 to 1. The system has the abundances species.n of the members of the group species, the growth growth, and the interactions triplets, whose tensor is the parameter triplets.a.

    IntrinsicInstabilitySystem(*, x=1.1, eta=0.1, alpha=0.01, beta=0.01, nu=0.01, p=0.001, sigma=0.01, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Jensen's coupled populations, whose steady state becomes unstable.

    It becomes unstable without a change of the surroundings.

    The resident population fluctuates about its level X = 1 until a rare mutation seeds the invader. The invader then grows by the factor 1 + beta per step and suppresses the resident, so the trajectory leaves the fixed point (X, 0) along its unstable direction, with eigenvalue beta, and the resident declines although no parameter has changed. The system has the populations populations.x and populations.y.

    Lotka-Volterra predation where both species are harvested.

    The harvest has a constant effort.

    The populations cycle around prey = (d + predator_harvest) / b and predators = (r - prey_harvest) / a, which are also their averages over a cycle.     MeadowCapacitySystem(width=40, height=40, *, cows=80, growth=0.2, bite=0.75, threshold=0.9, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Cows that graze a meadow for a summer of 25 weeks.

    It shows how many cows the meadow can carry.

    Every week the grass regrows logistically, each cow eats bite of the grass of its patch, and each cow moves to the nearest patch that no other cow occupies and whose grass reaches threshold. A cow that finds none dies. Without regrowth a cow grazes its first patch and 25 more over the summer, so the meadow feeds about width * height / 26 cows, and regrowth raises its carrying capacity. The cows graze the patches down at the same pace, so a herd above the capacity runs out of grown patches all at once and dies out within a week, instead of shrinking to the capacity. The system has the groups pasture and cows.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    width int

    The number of columns of the meadow.

    growth float

    bite float

    The grass a cow eats in a week.

    		 0.75
    threshold float

    The least grass a patch needs for a cow to move there.

    NeutralBiodiversitySystem(individuals=200, *, nu=0.01, species=1, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    A neutral community of constant size with speciation and drift.

    Its species arise by speciation and vanish by drift.

    Every species is transient, yet the number of species settles around S_N = sum_n theta / (theta + n) for n from 0 to N - 1, with theta = (N - 1) nu / (1 - nu), and the mean number of species of k individuals around phi_k = theta / k prod_j (N - j + 1) / (N - j + theta) for j from 1 to k. The system has the group community and the number richness of species.

    NeutralClusteringSystem(shape=64, *, n=10.0, alpha=1.0, beta=0.5, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Organisms that divide, die, and hop between patches on a periodic lattice.

    They gather in clusters.

    Births balance deaths, so the mean number of organisms per patch stays n while its variance grows. Without hops it grows as 2 alpha n t, so most patches empty while a few fill. Hops at the rate beta slow the growth to t^(1/2) in one dimension and ln t in two, so the clusters persist in low dimension although the mean density obeys a diffusion equation. The system has the numbers patches.n of organisms on the lattice patches, and their mean mean and variance variance over the patches.

    Parameters:

    shape int | Sequence[int]

    alpha float

    def regrow(self, agent: PastureView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Grow the grass by one week of logistic growth.

    Args:
        agent:
            The patch.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    del system
    agent.grass += agent.growth * agent.grass * (1 - agent.grass)

    PenaeidShrimpSystem(gut=0.5, biomass=1.0, *, ration=2.5, respiration=0.05, L_inf=29.9, K=0.013, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The growth of one penaeid shrimp from the juvenile stage.

    The growth is forced by the food and the water temperature.

    The individual ingests food up to a maximum ration set by its biomass and the water temperature, assimilates its gut content, respires, and spawns, while its gonads grow and its carapace length follows von Bertalanffy's curve L(t) = L_inf (1 - exp(-K t)) from zero, which nears its asymptote after six to eight months. The gut content settles near I / A_e, the ingestion over the assimilation efficiency.

    The coefficients are those of the listing of Bala et al. (2017). With them the respiration of a juvenile at 28 C, respiration exp(0.07 T) (phi B)^0.185, is about half its biomass per day, more than its maximum ration, so the total biomass declines slowly while the gonads and the length grow. The weight gain the source describes needs a lower respiration coefficient, such as 0.02. The system has the states shrimp.gut, shrimp.biomass, shrimp.gonads, and shrimp.length.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    gut float

    The initial gut content, in grams of dry weight.

    		 0.5
    biomass float

    		 1.0
    ration float

    The factor of the maximum ration, lower for males.

    respiration float

    The coefficient of the weight-specific respiration, per day.

    		 0.05

    The asymptotic carapace length, in millimetres.

    		 29.9

    PioneerGrowthInteraction(label, *, target, intermediate, climax, half_time=3.65, w_intermediate=0.32, w_climax=0.68)

    Bases: RateInteraction

    Michaelis-Menten regrowth of pioneer trees.

    The other groups suppress their input from seeds.

    Alone, the volume follows V(t) = V_mat t / (K_M + t) after a clear cut, which is dV/dt = V (V / V_mat - 2) / K_M + C V_mat / K_M with C = 1. The other groups reduce the factor C = 1 - w_I V_I / V_mat,I - w_C V_C / V_mat,C, with weights normalized to sum to one, and no lower than 0.

    label str

    The label of the interaction.

    PredatorPreyEventsInteraction(label, *, prey, predators, r=1.0, K=200.0, a=0.02, h=0.5, e=0.5, m=0.3, stochastic=True)

    Bases: Interaction

    Births, crowding, saturating predation, and deaths of prey and predators.

    They are events of single individuals.

    Prey are born at the rate r x and die of crowding at the rate r x^2 / K. Predators kill prey at the Holling type II rate a x y / (1 + a h x), are born at e times that rate, and die at the rate m y. In deterministic mode the rates drive the populations as differential equations.

    The carrying capacity of the prey.

    		 200.0

    QuotaPhytoplanktonElement(label, visual=None, *, Q=1.5, P=1.0, r_inf=1.0, q=1.0, vmax=2.0, g=1.0, R=1.0, d=0.1)

    Bases: Element

    Phytoplankton that grows on the nutrient stored in its cells.

    It is the phytoplankton of the Droop cell-quota system.

    The quota follows dQ/dt = vmax R / (g + R) - r_inf (1 - q / Q) Q, the Michaelis-Menten uptake from the external nutrient R less the dilution by growth, and the biomass dP/dt = r_inf (1 - q / Q) P - d P.

    RickerSystem(n=0.5, *, r=2.0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Ricker's map of a population in discrete generations, n' = r n exp(-n).

    It is chaotic for large r.

    The positive fixed point n = ln r is stable while 1 < r < e^2. Beyond e^2, about 7.39, it loses stability to a two-cycle, and further period doublings lead to chaos near r = 14.8. The size stays positive for every r. The system has the population population.n.

    RosenzweigMacArthurInteraction(label, *, prey, predators, kappa=0.01, eta=0.8, phi=0.1, phi_end=0.2, rate=0.0)

    Rosenzweig-MacArthur predation of fast prey by slow predators.

    The crowding of the prey grows at a constant rate.

    In units of the predators' time scale, kappa dx/dt = x (1 - phi x) - x y / (1 + eta x) and dy/dt = x y / (1 + eta x) - y. The crowding phi, the inverse of the prey's carrying capacity, rises at the rate rate from phi to phi_end and stays there.

    RosenzweigMacarthurSystem(prey=None, predators=None, *, kappa=0.01, eta=0.8, phi=None, phi_end=None, rate=0.002, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Fast prey and slow predators whose carrying capacity shrinks at a rate.

    A fast shrinking tips them.

    By default the crowding rises from eta (1 - eta) / (1 + eta) to 1 - eta, the range where the coexistence point at x = 1 / (1 - eta) is stable, and the run starts there. A slow rise lets the populations track the point, and a rise faster than about 0.0004 makes the prey collapse for a while before they return.

    In a collapse the prey fall to about 1e-30, far below any absolute tolerance, and an error of either sign there decides whether they return or, below zero, run into the pole of the feeding at x = -1 / eta. The registered solver therefore controls the relative error only, with ScipyODESolver(rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-300). The system has the populations prey and predators.

    SequentiallyLinearEcosystemSystem(n=60, k=4, *, rate=0.2, threshold=0.001, seed=1, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    An ecosystem with linear dynamics between extinctions that rewrite its network.

    Every species reads k random species through influences of random sign and strength, and grows linearly with their abundances. Between extinctions the dynamics is linear, so the abundances approach the dominant eigenvector of the current network. A species whose abundance falls below threshold goes extinct with its influences, and a new species with k random influences takes its place, which changes the network and starts a new linear stretch. Extinctions come in bursts separated by quiet periods. The system has the abundances species.x and ages species.age of the variable group species and the strengths influences.w of the variable group influences on the edges.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    n int

    The number of species.

    		 60
    k int

    The number of species every species reads.

    		 4
    rate float

    The growth per step per unit of influence.

    		 0.2
    threshold float

    The abundance below which a species goes extinct.

    		 0.001
    seed int | None

    The seed of the network and of the initial strengths.

    		 1
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    ShrimpElement(label, visual=None, *, gut=0.5, biomass=1.0, gonads=0.0001, length=0.0, ration=2.5, k=0.12, assimilation=0.8, respiration=0.05, phi=5.0, gsi=0.05, egg_weight=2e-06, L_inf=29.9, K=0.013)

    Bases: Element

    Penaeid shrimp, an individual that grows on food at the water temperature.

    Its gut, biomass, gonads, and length grow.

    The shrimp ingests I = R_max (1 - exp(-k F)) of the food F, with the maximum ration R_max the product of a table of its biomass, a table of the water temperature, and the factor ration. Its gut content G follows dG/dt = I - A_e G, and its total biomass dB/dt = A_e G - M - S, with the respiration M = a exp(0.07 T) (phi B)^0.185 B and the spawning S = 9.3 L^2.8 E_w of eggs of weight E_w. Its gonads grow as dB_g/dt = GSI B, and its carapace length follows von Bertalanffy, dL/dt = K (L_inf - L). The food and the water temperature are the yearly series of the source, interpolated linearly in days.

    StigmergicPredatorPreySystem(width=30, height=30, *, plants=300, prey=120, predators=20, emotions=True, decay=0.2, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Plants, prey, and predators on a grid.

    The animals share emotions through decaying marks.

    Every cell holds at most one organism. Prey eat plants and fear predators, and predators eat prey and grow angry with hunger. Happiness draws animals of the same kind towards the cells where it was marked and distress drives them away, a trail stigmergy of emotions that the cellular automaton of Olsen in Carmichael and Hadžikadić (2019) uses to study cooperation within each species. The system has the groups life/plants, life/prey, and life/predators, and the marks ground/marks.

    decay float

    The rate at which the marks decay.

    The seed or generator of the initial cells.

    		 'system'

>>> system = StigmergicPredatorPreySystem(10, 10, plants=20, prey=10, predators=5).prepare().system_

    StochasticPredatorPreySystem(prey=200.0, predators=200.0, *, r=1.0, K=600.0, a=0.005, h=0.5, e=0.5, m=0.3, stochastic=True, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Prey and predators born and killed one at a time.

    The prey crowd and the predation saturates.

    The deterministic limit has the coexistence point x = m / (a (e - m h)). It is stable while K < 2 x + 1 / (a h), and enriching the prey beyond that turns it into large cycles, which demographic noise drives to extinction. The system has the populations prey and predators.

    TripletInteraction(label, *, target, a=0.0, state='x')

    Bases: RateInteraction

    Interactions of every species with the pairs of other species.

    They add dx_i/dt += x_i sum_(j<k) a_ijk x_j x_k.

    The coefficient a_ijk is the effect of the combination of the species j and k on the growth of the species i (Sidhom and Galla 2024, Eq. 2). The tensor holds it for both orders of the pair, a_ijk = a_ikj, so the sum over the sets j < k is half the contraction of the tensor with the abundances, and it holds 0 where indices coincide.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the interaction.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

    The path of the group of species.

    		 required
    a Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(shape=(target, target, target))]

    The coupling tensor of order 3, with one index per species, or a number for every entry.

    		 0.0
    state str

    The name of the state that holds the abundance of a species.

    		 'x'

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import TripletInteraction
>>> TripletInteraction('triplets', target='species', a=0.0, state='n').state

    UnstablePopulationsElement(label, visual=None, *, x=1.1, y=0.0, eta=0.1, mean=1.0, alpha=0.01, beta=0.01, nu=0.01, p=0.001, sigma=0.01)

    Bases: Element

    Resident population x and invading population y.

    They follow equations (13.3) and (13.4) of Jensen.

    The maps of IntrinsicInstabilitySystem step both sizes. At every step x ← [x - eta (x - X)] exp(-alpha y) + √x sigma chi, an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck step damped by the invader. With probability p a mutation from x adds nu x to y, and otherwise y ← y (1 + beta) + √y sigma chi'. The noises chi and chi' are independent standard normal values, scaled by the square root of the population sizes as in birth and death processes, and both sizes are cut at 0.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the populations.

    		 required
    visual VisualSpec | None

    How the element is drawn, or None for default_visual_.

    		 None
    x Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The initial resident population.

    		 1.1
    y Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The initial invading population.

    		 0.0
    eta Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The restoring rate eta of the resident population.

    		 0.1
    mean Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The level X the resident population returns to.

    		 1.0
    alpha Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The suppression alpha of the resident population by the invader.

    		 0.01
    beta Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The growth rate beta of the invader.

    		 0.01
    nu Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The share nu of the resident population that a mutation moves to the invader.

    		 0.01
    p Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The probability of a mutation per step.

    		 0.001
    sigma Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The amplitude sigma of the noise.

    		 0.01

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import UnstablePopulationsElement
>>> UnstablePopulationsElement('populations').p
0.001

    VaryingCapacityLogisticSystem(n=10.0, *, r=2.0, K=100.0, amplitude=0.5, period=1.0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Logistic growth under a seasonal carrying capacity.

    It settles on a cycle of the season's period.

    Whatever its initial size, the population tends to a unique periodic solution, which lags behind the capacity and varies less than it. The system has the population population.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    n float

    The initial size.

    		 10.0
    r float

    The intrinsic growth rate.

    		 2.0
    K float

    The mean carrying capacity.

    		 100.0
    amplitude float

    The relative amplitude of the seasonal variation of the capacity, below 1.

    		 0.5
    period float

    The period of the seasons.

    		 1.0
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import VaryingCapacityLogisticSystem
>>> VaryingCapacityLogisticSystem(amplitude=0.2).prepare().system_.interactions[0].amplitude
0.2

    WolfElement(label, visual=VisualSpec('agents', {'radius': 0.35}), *, energy=20.0, gain=20.0, reproduction=0.05)

    Bases: Element

    Wolf that wanders, eats a sheep, reproduces, and dies without energy.

    In its own activation, a wolf wanders to a neighbouring cell at a cost of one unit of energy, eats and removes one random sheep of its cell, and dies below zero energy or gives birth with probability reproduction, by member interactions.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the agent or group.

    		 required
    visual VisualSpec | None

    How the element is drawn, or None for default_visual_.

    		 VisualSpec('agents', {'radius': 0.35})
    energy Annotated[float, StateSpec()]

    The initial energy.

    		 20.0
    gain Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The energy a wolf gains from a sheep.

    		 20.0
    reproduction Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The probability of reproducing at every step.

    		 0.05

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import WolfElement
>>> GroupElement('wolves', element=WolfElement, size=25).size
25
